question: How much observed gain does bounded recalibration offer over reusing a stopping condition after replacing the downstream policy bundle?

scope.normalizers: Each checkpoint retains its own pinned normalizer
no_claim: true optimal-setting regret from a finite selected comparator

candidates.selection: first crossing of horizontal base-target distance <= r and yaw condition; do not replace trajectory by teleport
candidates.hold: base zero velocity, preserve current arm/trunk and gripper commands; no keep_still for objects

selection_rule.data: 4 calibration sources x 3 candidates for each policy
rank: maximum end-to-end successes incl navigation failures
minimum sum of actual navigation+hold+pickup control ticks over ALL 4 calibration attempts for each candidate
selection_rule.all_zero: NO_OBSERVED_SUCCESS; fixed 0.9 fallback, not optimal A/B selection
selection_rule.any_technical_missing: INCOMPLETE_CALIBRATION; no data-driven selection; fixed 0.9 fallback labelled
selection_rule.a_unselectable: Do not report transfer of an A-calibrated optimum

roles.group: one shared scene-instance template; source paths distinct, physical independence unverified
roles.seed_binding: Design choice only; native manifest must bind simulator, policy and controller RNG. No runtime packet rewritten.

counterfactual_capture.same_candidate: Run one common navigation+hold prefix then restore full identical state for A/B. Candidate-specific prefix is shared across policies only.
counterfactual_capture.across_candidates: Different stopping trajectories/states are intentionally part of the intervention; do not claim identical post-navigation states across k.
counterfactual_capture.reference: Demo skill1 snapshot is a separate competence diagnostic, never the common arrived state

outcome.Y: navigation condition reached within budget AND pickup grasped predicate first-hit within budget
outcome.primary_rate: verified Y=1 / all prespecified starts with unresolved count separately
outcome.grasp_semantics: General BDDL grasp success is not automatically right-gripper adherence or stable grasp; report separately.

estimands.true_transfer_regret: max_k mu_B(k)-mu_B(k_A_hat); generally not identified by the finite selected k_B_hat comparator
estimands.negative_reselection: Allowed: finite calibration may choose poorly. Do not clamp negative estimates to zero.
estimands.interaction: (meanY_B(k1)-meanY_B(k2))-(meanY_A(k1)-meanY_A(k2)); descriptive sensitivity, not geometry-only causal effect
estimands.no_leakage: Never select k_B from evaluation or report best test candidate as observed primary benefit
estimands.same_choice: k_A_hat == k_B_hat reuses the same recorded B outcome for both logical arms; report zero contrast and spent selection cost. Do not manufacture a setting effect from independent stochastic reruns of that identical arm.

cost.scope: Prior future design estimate only; P0 unchanged; no execution authorization
cost.actual: Count unique physical runs once; tag logical reuse and amortization separately
cost.selection_tie_cost: All four attempts, including failed/no-arrival consumed ticks; not success-only duration
cost.deployment: Report calibration robot time and computation alongside per-task deployment cost. No arbitrary success-to-GPU-time conversion.

statistical_scope.mandatory: Raw policy x candidate cells, selected choices, paired gains, missingness bounds and per-source outcomes; no retrospective threshold tuning

counterexamples_reviewed: Different finite calibration winners can arise without different true policy rankings
A uniformly weaker B is not by itself stopping-condition transfer loss
Different stopping thresholds can produce identical actual stop states
A fast failed attempt can win a tick tie; log the full success/tick table rather than describing it as better motion
All-zero or incomplete calibration cannot substantiate optimal-setting reuse
remaining_dependencies: actual policy competence and physical state duplication
effect comparison within the declared limited population
